docs.api.intro: Scope, channels and PIN are the annotations of `docs/contracts/scopes.md`, checked by the server against the definitions. By default the channels are the owner's four (the web page, a paired device, the command line, a token the external issuer signed for the owner); a token the external issuer signed for someone else can never call the local API (only the A2A entry); an AI's working credential can only call routes marked “AI (own session only)”. The AI's own tools (`daisy:tools`: timed wake-ups, recurring tasks, background commands, speaking up) are offered over MCP, not the local API, and are not in this table; the one exception is fetching a token for the AI (`session.aiToken`), which the MCP inside the harness calls with the turn's AI working credential.

docs.cli.intro:
This page lists every `{command}` command; each block is exactly what `{command} <command> --help` prints.

There are two kinds of commands:

- **Local commands** manage the {product} process and files on this machine; they work while {product} is not running.
- **API commands** call the running {product} through the local API. Everything the web page can do is here, except answering the AI's tool approvals and questions (only on the web page and paired devices).

A few rules hold for all of them:

- Commands marked “needs the PIN” prompt for the PIN in the terminal first.
- Credentials (PIN, API key, authorization code) are read from a prompt or standard input, never from the command line, so they stay out of the shell history.
- API commands print their answer as JSON on standard output; on an error they say what happened and what to do, and exit non-zero.
- The global option `--data-dir <dir>` (or the `DAISY_DATA` environment variable) picks another data directory; `--lang <language>` (or `DAISY_LANG`) another language.

The HTTP API behind the API commands is in the [local API reference](../../api/local-api.md).
